Neither Bloch original nor complete Gaddis book inspected; no literal time-travel or experimental-replication claim.

proposals.relationship: Refers to Benjamin’s Illuminations as a comparable artistic metaphor for the historian’s backward-looking perspective.
proposals.evidence_note: Specific own first-chapter note4, attached to the historian’s back-turned posture, identifies Illuminations, Harry Zohn translation, NewYork1968,p257. A bounded conceptual comparison used by Gaddis, not formal mentorship or direct inspection of Benjamin’s German text. The source’s particular reverse-facing image is not generalized to agreement with Benjamin’s philosophy of history.
primary_locators: First-chapter opening paragraph ending a rear end; note4

proposals.relationship: Criticizes The Cold War: A New History for a US-centered triumphalist narrative that marginalizes other societies, culture and continuing legacies.
proposals.evidence_note: Own signed2006review sections1–3 targets a particular popular book: Soviet perspectives, ThirdWorld costs, differences among WesternEuropeans and cultural/generational conflict, plus connections after1989. Judt acknowledges Gaddis’s earlier archival achievements and treats We Now Know as a different work. No claim that Judt discovered every alleged factual error correctly or that this exhausts Gaddis’s scholarship; complete reviewed book unread.
primary_locators: Review sections1–3, especially paragraphs beginning Any history, As a result, The cold war was experienced, and To ignore the prehistory
